### Who Will Be King?
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/who-will-be-king
Passage: 1 Kings 1:20
Points:
- As King David's health deteriorated, his son Adonijah exploited the situation to seize the throne.
- Adonijah's celebratory banquet deliberately omitted Nathan and Solomon, signaling his intent to eliminate them.
- Nathan and Bathsheba recognized the imminent danger and approached David to remind him of his pledge concerning Solomon.
- Instead of passively waiting for God to intervene, they took decisive, wise initiative to preserve the kingdom.
- God's sovereign promises do not eliminate the necessity of prudent, faithful action by His people.

### Day 80: 1 Kings 1:11–31
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-80-1-kings-1-1131.html
Passage: 1 Kings 1:11–31
Points:
- Nathan proved to be a faithful prophet by showing compassionate care to David and Bathsheba years after confronting their sin.
- Recognizing Bathsheba's unique influence with the king, Nathan sent her to report Adonijah's coup and followed to confirm it.
- Bathsheba warned David that she and Solomon faced death as traitors if Adonijah succeeded in his rebellion.
- Facing this urgent crisis stirred the frail king to fulfill his promise and execute God's will.
- Authentic spiritual leaders combine the courage to address past sin with the grace to stand alongside people in crisis.
